newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gold plan brings inflation risks-German "wise man".
newsitem.headline: Gold plan brings inflation risks-German "wise man".

text.p: A key economic advisor to the German government said on Friday a plan to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves carried inflation risks and should be seen as a measure never to be repeated.

Rolf Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisors dubbed Germany's "Five Wise Men", said on German radio that Finance Minister Theo Waigel should above all only use a small part of any revaluation windfall for budgetary ends.
"I see the crucial problem as being the setting-in-motion of the inflation process," Peffekoven said.
He added that any Bundesbank profit emerging from an upwards revaluation of its bullion reserves would "create (a corresponding amount of) additional money" that would entail inflation risks.

Peffekoven put the potential profit available from a full valuation of Bundesbank gold at current market prices at some 43 billion marks. Of that, only some seven billion should be used towards the budget, he said.
The rest should go towards offsetting historic debt associated with German unification, he said.
Peffekoven stressed that the revaluation of reserves was something that could be done "precisely once" and should not be repeated in coming years.
